title: Interplay with Financial Services Rules and Data Protection
summary: How AI Act obligations integrate with internal governance, model risk, consumer credit, insurance distribution and DORA requirements, and with the GDPR's rules on automated decision-making and impact assessments.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How AI Act obligations integrate with internal governance, model risk, consumer credit, insurance distribution and DORA requirements, and with the GDPR's rules on automated decision-making and impact assessments.
Learning Objectives: Map AI Act obligations onto existing financial services governance requirements
Apply the provisions that let financial firms meet obligations through internal governance rules
Align AI Act compliance with the GDPR, including automated decisions and DPIAs
Syllabus: Quality management and monitoring through internal governance arrangements
Consumer credit, insurance distribution and conduct rules applied to AI
GDPR: lawful basis, automated decision-making and DPIAs alongside FRIAs
Model risk management, outsourcing and DORA as complementary frameworks
Intended Audience: Supervisors, policy and innovation staff at national competent authorities responsible for AI used by financial entities
Compliance, risk, legal, data protection and model risk staff at banks, insurers, investment firms and payment firms
Senior managers and directors accountable for the firm's use of AI and its AI Act compliance
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with how AI or models are used in financial services is helpful. No technical or legal background is required.
Core Reading: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (General Data Protection Regulation)
OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)
